newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico novelist Fuentes slams U.S."xenophobia".
newsitem.headline: Mexico novelist Fuentes slams U.S."xenophobia".

text.p: Mexican novelist Carlos Fuentes has lashed out at what he called U.S. xenophobia and fascism against Mexican migrants.

Fuentes was particularly scathing in a speech on Tuesday night about the latest U.S. immigration and welfare laws that crack down on illegal immigrants and cut welfare benefits to those who are legal.

"This a huge demagogical and political farce being staged by some U.S. politicians," Fuentes said in a speech accepting an award as Commander of the National Order of Merit at the French Embassy in Mexico City.
"They know they need migrant Mexican labour, without which their harvests, services and many aspects of life would go to ruin," he said.

"What would become of California and the United States without Mexican workers? They need us... The rest is demagogy, the triumph of certain xenophobic and fascist feelings that abound in the United States... but the bottom line is that the U.S. economy cannot function without Mexican workers," he said.

Fuentes latest novel, "La Frontera de Cristal" (The Crystal Frontier), deals with the issue of U.S.-Mexican relations from the point of view of an extended family spanning both sides of the Rio Grande border river.

When asked what the effects of the recent changes in U.S. legislation would have on migrant workers such as his fictional character Benito Ayala, Fuentes said this would not stem the demand for cheap labour.

Fuentes said Mexicans picked 90 percent of agricultural produce in California, which grows one-third of the U.S. total. "Migrant workers do not take jobs from any one...they pay thirty times more taxes than they receive in benefits", he said.

Latin America traditionally pays great heed to the words of its writers and intellectuals on the political issues of the day and Fuentes has previously appeared in workshops organised by Mexico's political opposition.
